statements.impact_statement: CVE-2007-2768 lets a remote client find out whether a user account exists when sshd authenticates through the OPIE one-time-password PAM module, because OPIE answers with a different challenge for accounts that exist (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2007-2768, https://bugs.debian.org/436571, which points to the OPIE report https://bugs.debian.org/112279). The differing response comes from the OPIE PAM module, not from OpenSSH, and Debian removed its libpam-opie package from the archive in 2011 (https://bugs.debian.org/112279). The DHI Debian repository publishes three builds of openssh for Debian 13, all rebuilds of Debian's 1:10.0p1-7+deb13u4. We checked the openssh-server and openssh-server-dbgsym packages of all three on amd64 and arm64, verified against the index checksums: sshd, sshd-session and sshd-auth contain no OPIE code or strings, while in every build the same searches find the OpenSSH_10.0 version string in all three and the PAM function sshpam_init_ctx in the debug symbols of sshd-session and sshd-auth, which handle authentication. No OPIE package is published in the DHI Debian repository.
